content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure and function of the endocrine system
Identify the main endocrine glands and their hormones
Explain how hormones affect target organs
Compare the endocrine system with the nervous system

is a collection of glands that produce hormones to regulate body functions. Unlike the nervous system which uses electrical impulses, the endocrine system uses chemical messengers (hormones) that travel through the blood. It controls slower, longer-lasting processes such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
Collection of glands throughout the body
Hormones travel in blood to target organs
Works with nervous system for coordination
